title: Layerwise adaptivity calibration and stability hardening for FP8 enablement on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Safely enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles for a subset of Hopper-backed models used in hosted and dedicated modes by introducing a layerwise-adaptive calibration step, per-op hysteresis safeguards, and a telemetry-driven rollback mesh. This ticket coordinates engineering work to build a deterministic calibration transfer mechanism (shadow replays), an activation gate that evaluates per-layer sensitivity at runtime, and automated canary checks tied to quality/regression thresholds.

Background: Prior FP8 enablement work showed intermittent accuracy regressions correlated with specific attention/FFN layers and sequence-length distributions. Current calibration pipeline applies a global scale per-tensor which underfits some high-variance ops. We need a more granular approach that remains robust across traffic distributions and compatible with autoscaling in Dedicated.

Scope:
- Implement "layerwise adaptivity": compute per-layer scale/stats during offline calibration and maintain a lightweight runtime adjustment factor using cached calibration deltas.
- Build shadow-replay calibration transfer: replay representative micro-batches in shadow mode against a candidate FP8 profile to detect layer-level mismatch before activation.
- Add per-op hysteresis and temporal smoothing to prevent oscillation under bursty traffic.
- Expand telemetry to include layer-level delta histograms, per-sequence-length error percentiles, and per-profile FN/FP quality gates.
- Define automated canary checks and circuit-breaker thresholds for rollback.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Granularity vs. latency: per-layer adjustments add a small runtime cost (measured ~0.6–1.2% token latency on hopper-large). We accepted this for P0 customers but exposed a config flag to disable adaptivity for ultra-low-latency tiers.
- Complexity vs. coverage: shadow replays increase traffic and storage for cached activations. We constrained replay sample size and prioritized high-impact routes (top 5 by token volume) to limit cost.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Layerwise+Adaptivity+for+FP8 (internal)
- Calibration harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345
- Canary orchestration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestration/pull/5432
- Grafana dashboard (telemetry): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/FP8-calib/Layerwise-stats
- Eval suite: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Fp8-eval-suite
- Slack thread: #quantization (thread TS: 1678923456.000200)

Safety/rollback plan:
- Primary rollback triggers: end-to-end accuracy drop > 0.6% on golden prompt set OR layer-level DL2 error spike > 2x baseline OR regression alerts from production QA canary.
- Canary flow: dark-launch FP8 profile to 1% traffic (shadow replays enabled). If canary passes, progressive rollout to 10%, 30%, 60% with telemetry gates at each step.
- Emergency action: automatic demote to compatible INT8 profile + alert to on-call + create postmortem ticket.

Validation strategy:
- Golden prompt set with weighted customer traffic distribution to validate quality not just average accuracy but tail behavior.
- Per-layer A/B delta vectors: compute logit/k-L divergence at layer outputs for representative batches.
- Long-tail fuzzing for sequence lengths (8,32,128,1024), focusing on KV cache boundary behavior.

Risks and mitigations:
- Drift after calibration due to model updates: add a nightly micro-calibration run and a freshness score that gates activation.
- Non-deterministic kernels on certain driver versions: we added a driver compatibility matrix and flagged unsupported combos; runtime will fallback to INT8 for those shards.
- Telemetry volume: downsample and store histograms instead of raw per-request traces for layer stats.

Deliverables:
- Calibration library changes (PR linked) + unit/integration tests.
- Shadow-replay controller and sampling config.
- Canary orchestration changes to support layer-level gates.
- New Grafana dashboards and Alert rules.
- Runbook for on-call and rollout checklist.

Notes:
- Early tests on internal hopper-dev cluster (hdev-6) show acceptable stability at 10% traffic for Llama-2-13B with E5M2 profile after adding per-layer smoothing. We observed a 0.12% average delta and 0.8% max tail delta across sequence lengths.
- Observed pathological case: short prompts (~<12 tokens) with self-attention patterns produced amplified per-op scaling noise. Mitigation: explicit short-seq calibration bucket and stronger hysteresis threshold for head attention ops.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish integration tests and automate replay sampling selection (owner: Marco).
- Deploy canary to hosted-dev and run 72h soak (owner: Aisha).
- Coordinate with SRE to provision a dedicated shadow-capacity queue for replays to avoid impacting production latency (owner: Priya Rao).

If blockers arise, escalate to Quantization Guild for prioritization and to Runtime team for kernel fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration library computes per-layer scale deltas and stores in profile artifact
Shadow-replay controller can run representative micro-batches and flag layer-level mismatches
Automated canary rollout passes three consecutive gates on hosted-dev and dedicated-staging
Dashboards show layer-level delta histograms and alerts fire at configured thresholds
On-call runbook documented and tested in a dry-run
